rows.question: Can a Subclass 417 Working Holiday visa holder work for the same employer for more than 6 months in the tourism and hospitality sector?
rows.gold_answer: Yes — tourism and hospitality is a listed critical sector exemption to the 6-month same-employer limitation (condition 8547), so no permission is needed.
rows.rag_answer: No, a Subclass 417 Working Holiday visa holder cannot work for the same employer for more than 6 months. This is due to visa condition 8547, which imposes a requirement to rotate employer or location every 6 months, unless an exemption applies. For further details, refer to the WHM 6 month work limitation document.

rows.question: What is condition 8547 and which visa holders does it apply to?
rows.gold_answer: Condition 8547 is the 6-month work limitation with the same employer. It applies to anyone holding a Working Holiday Maker (WHM) visa, including subclass 417 and 462, and to bridging visa holders with the condition attached.
rows.rag_answer: Condition 8547 — WHM 6 month work limitation — applies to anyone in Australia who holds a Working Holiday Maker (WHM) visa, specifically Subclass 417 (Working Holiday) or Subclass 462 (Work and Holiday). This includes individuals arriving with these visas as well as those holding a Bridging visa with condition 8547 imposed. The condition applies to any type of work unless an exemption applies. Source: whm_6_month_work_limitation.txt

rows.question: I'm on a Working Holiday visa doing fruit picking on a farm — do I need permission to keep working for the same farm after 8 months?
rows.gold_answer: No — plant and animal cultivation (including harvesting/packing fruit and vegetable crops) is an exempt category under condition 8547, so no permission is needed to continue past 6 months.
